phases.title: Setup
phases.goal: A working toolchain and one scratch project you'll add every exercise to.
sources: Getting Started with .net 8.0 with C# for crestron in Visual studio 2022.pdf
4-Series and VC-4 C# Development Instructions-Mar2021.pdf, MCP-101 VC-4 Program Load HowTo.pdf

tasks.text: Read Tim's .NET 8 getting-started PDF and the MCP-101 VC-4 program load how-to
Install VS 2022, .NET 8 SDK, and the `Crestron.SimplSharp.SDK.Program` NuGet
Get a VC-4 instance you can deploy to (.NET 8 runs on VC-4, not on 4-Series hardware)
Install Node + `@crestron/ch5-shell-utilities-cli` for CH5 projects
Clone M26, build the backend, deploy to VC-4 and confirm it loads
Create your `StudyLab` SIMPL# Pro project; every exercise becomes a console command or class in it

phases.title: C# foundations & program lifecycle
phases.goal: The C# features Crestron code leans on, and the rules for constructor vs InitializeSystem.

tasks.text: TIM 205 Casting and 271 CheckingForNull. Relate to analog ↔ percent and `?.` / `??` in M26
TIM 303_304 AccessModifiers. Why is every M26 class `internal` or `sealed`?
TIM 311a Delegates, 311b CustomEventArgs, 320 BasicLambda
Write `ProjectorEventArgs` (PowerState, LampHours), raise it from a fake projector, subscribe twice, unsubscribe once
TIM 317_318 Timers/Delay/Async. Write a 3 s delay three ways and note which one blocks
Spot the bugs in TIM 319 `MyWorker` (unsafe queue, busy-wait, non-volatile flag, finalizer), then fix with a blocking queue
MCP-101 ControlSystem comments: what's allowed in the constructor vs `InitializeSystem`, and why both must return fast
Make `StudyLab.ControlSystem` a `partial class` and move System/Program/Ethernet handlers into `ControlSystemEvents.cs`
TIM 323 Reflection with interfaces (you'll need it again in Phase 7)

phases.title: Files & JSON
phases.goal: Move room data out of code: read, deserialize, use, change, serialize, write back.
sources: instructor note/Instructor-Guide.md (Modules 1–6), Student-Cheat-Sheet.md, docs/, Config/RoomConfig.cs, Config/PresetStore.cs

tasks.text: M26 guide Modules 1–3 and the cheat sheet. Do the spot-the-error JSON exercise by hand
Compare `docs/sample-roomconfig.json` with `.xml`, then the MSS-431 XML config vs the MSS-421 JSON config
TIM 433 FilePaths: app folder, `/user`, `/nvram`, `/rm`. Then read how M26 picks `/user` vs VC-4 app root
TIM 434a ReadingFiles: whole file vs line-by-line, `using` blocks
M26 Modules 4–5: map every JSON key in `RoomConfig.cs`; compare `[JsonPropertyName]` with `PresetStore`'s CamelCase policy
Recreate TIM 435 (`SeedData`/`WriteJSON`/`ReadJSON`/`AddRoom`) with System.Text.Json
Add `roomconfig` (dump) and `roomreload` (re-read) console commands
Break the JSON on purpose (comment, trailing comma, single quotes, `True`) and record what System.Text.Json says. Which one passes because of `AllowTrailingCommas`?
TIM DataStore example: when would you choose DataStore over a JSON file?
Model one of your real jobs as JSON (projector IP/port, Aver presets, NVX IP-IDs, sources) and write the classes

phases.title: Robustness: surviving the real world
phases.goal: Power loss, thread collisions, bad files: the room must still come up.

tasks.text: Read `ConfigManager.Load()` and list every fallback path
Deadlock demo: move `_lock.Leave()` out of `finally`, throw, call Load twice. Then restore
Move `ConfigChanged?.Invoke` inside the lock with a subscriber that calls `Load()`, and explain the result
Enable auto-update and edit the file over SFTP while watching the panel update
Add `ConfigManager.Save()`: lock, write `.tmp`, replace, release in `finally`
Give `PresetStore.Save()` the same temp-then-swap and a try/catch in `Load()`
TIM DataStore: find the `&` vs `|` flags bug and the `GLobalString` typo
MSS-421 `Config.Load/Save`: unused XmlSerializer, double open, undisposed reader, non-atomic save. Rewrite it properly

phases.title: UI: joins → frameworks → contracts
phases.goal: From raw join numbers to a production-grade contract UI handler.
sources: InstructorCompletedExercise ControlSystem.cs (join enums), Building a UI Framework/TPBase.cs

tasks.text: MSS-431 join enums (`enum Buttons { Settings = 1 … }`) and why they beat magic numbers
MSS-431 `TPBase`: `handleBtn` / `handleRange` with press/release filtering
Refactor TIM `Touchpanel.cs` to accept any `BasicTriListWithSmartObject` (answers Tim's own question)
Create panels from the JSON config at startup (config-driven panel list)
TIM Modern Contract example homework: wire the Apple TV D-pad and transport
TIM ContractWidgetList: item count, `_Indirect` text, per-item events
Do the MSS-521 subpage lab yourself (`ShowMainSubpages`) before reading the answer
M26 `UiHandler`: list five things that make it production-ready
Add `System.RoomName` to M26 end to end: Contract Editor → `.g.cs` → C# → Angular

phases.title: CH5 front-end
phases.goal: Angular/React panels that are wired cleanly and look good on a wall panel.

tasks.text: CH5 `WebXPanel.ts`: `runsInContainerApp`, URL query config, the four events
CH5 `CrestronRouterService`: control system pulses a visibility join → router navigates; default page at startup
CH5 `volume.component.ts`: `subscribeState` + `ngZone.run` + signals + `unsubscribeState` in `ngOnDestroy`
Compare the React `CrComLibContext` with the Angular service approach
Build and run `mux-521-angular-complete` in a browser as a WebXPanel (`?host=&ipid=&port=`)
Port the CH5 d-pad/o-pad components into the M26 frontend, wired to M26's contract
Restyle the M26 frontend with its CSS tokens for a real panel size (TSW-770 1280×800)
Full pipeline: `ng build` → `ch5-cli archive` → `ch5-cli deploy` to VC-4 / a panel

phases.title: Architecture: gluing it all together
phases.goal: The same room programmed three ways, so you can choose a structure on purpose.
sources: Message Broker Solution-Tim/ (MessageBroker, Nvx3xx, Airmedia3100, CrestronConnected, Automation.cs, DeviceSetup.cs, SimpleEventTimers2.cs)
root program (the 2024 version of the same room)

tasks.text: Read the MSS-621 READMEs: the room (AirMedia, NVX as switcher + global streams, Apple TV IR, Connected display)
Jeremy's solution: `ControlSystem.global`, `SystemPower` setter, `Audio` base class with `virtual` methods
Mark's `Dom.cs` vs his MessageBroker: why the broker exists
Tim's solution: `DeviceSetup` wrappers → `Automation` (room logic only) → `UI/` (presses and page flips only)
Tim's `Nvx.cs` wrapper: own enums, defaults in constructor, `ComPorts[1]` (1-based), IR port reuse, XML docs
Find the bugs: `GetNvxAddress` off-by-one, `AddEvent` ignoring params, `LogusMaximus` dropping msg2, broker not thread-safe
Write a thread-safe broker (lock, `Invoke`, try/catch per send, key constants) plus a `brokermon` command
Build your own device wrapper library DLL (e.g. `PanasonicProjector`) and reference it from `StudyLab`
Write a one-page decision note: which of the three styles will you use for your jobs, and why

phases.title: Device comms & drivers
phases.goal: Talk to real devices reliably, and load Crestron drivers at runtime.

tasks.text: MCP-101 `TCPClientHelper`: worker thread + `CrestronQueue`, and the codepage 1252 vs 28591 lesson
List what `TCPClientHelper` gets wrong (whole-buffer decode, spin loop, no reconnect) and write a fixed version
TIM 450: trace `PowerOn` from driver JSON → `PrepareStringThenSend` → `ValidateResponse` → `DeConstructPower`
MSS-431 reflection plugin: shared interface DLL + `Assembly.LoadFrom`
MSS-521 driver demo: unzip `.pkg`, find `IBasicVideoDisplay` + `ITcp`, `Initialize`, `StateChangeEvent`, `Connect`
Run the MSS-521 driver demo against its built-in TCP emulator (or TIM 450's projector emulator)
Write a Panasonic projector protocol class (power, input, power poll) behind an `IDisplay` interface
Swap M26's `DeviceEmulator` display side for your `IDisplay` with no UI changes

phases.title: Web, tools & discovery
phases.goal: Browser settings pages over CWS, debugging on VC-4, and bus/network discovery.
sources: CWSDebug.cs, Config.cs (Cws method), WebFolder/app.js + settings.html + debug.html
Cresnet Helper Example, Ethernet Discovery Example

tasks.text: MSS-421 CWS: `HttpCwsServer`, `HttpCwsRoute` with `{TOKEN}`, `IHttpCwsHandler`, root event for query strings
MSS-421 `app.js`: the VC-4 `../cws/` path gotcha
Serve your `roomConfig.json` over CWS (GET + PUT) with a small settings page, locked and written atomically
Add a CWS debug log (rolling 50 messages) like `CWSDebug`
Start MCP-101 `VirtualConsole` on VC-4 (open the host firewall port) and add a command
Mark's VC-4 log tip: `sudo grep "SimplSharpPro" /var/log/messages`
MSS-431 Ethernet discovery: list devices; note why TSW IP tables need SSH
MSS-431 Cresnet discovery (if you have Cresnet): run it on a thread and keep assigned IDs stable

phases.title: Security & code review
phases.goal: Find what the examples leave open, and review your own code the same way.

tasks.text: MSS-521 driver upload: path traversal via `X-File-Name`, unauthenticated DLL load, double response. Write the hardened version
MSS-421/431 `Password`: hard-coded salt, SHA-1/1000 iterations, non-constant compare. Rewrite with a random salt, PBKDF2-SHA256, `FixedTimeEquals`
Add authentication to your CWS settings page from Phase 8
Make debug consoles and pages switchable off for production builds
Ask Claude to run the `crestron-code-review` skill on your `StudyLab` and fix every finding

phases.title: Capstone room program
phases.goal: Your own room, no copying. Refer back only when stuck.

tasks.text: `roomConfig.json`: room, panels, sources, displays (type + IP), camera presets
ConfigManager with lock, atomic save, safe load and auto-reload; presets in a separate file
Your chosen architecture (Phase 6) with device wrapper DLLs
Contract UI + CH5 panel from Phase 5, with offline start page and full feedback on reconnect
Display via `IDisplay`: emulator first, then your Panasonic driver
CWS settings page with auth; debug off in production
Clean shutdown: timers stopped, handlers disposed, sockets closed
Final test: restart mid-save, corrupt the JSON, unplug the panel, drop the projector. The room must recover
Full review with the `crestron-code-review` skill, then write the README
